lessons.description: Netilas Yadayim LiSeudah 6 - Parshas Devarim - Nafilim - Sichon - Og - 515 prayers of Moshe Rabbeinu - Speaker: Rabbi Nasan Maimon. Hilkhos Netilas Yadayim LiSeudah 6 is based on 2Likutey Moharan 7 . 00:00 - This shiur is dedicated l'ilui nishmas (for the elevation of the soul) of Rabbi Ozer b'Reb Alexander HaKohen Ber
lessons.bodyText: Netilas Yadayim LiSeudah 6 - Parshas Devarim - Nafilim - Sichon - Og - 515 prayers of Moshe Rabbeinu - Speaker: Rabbi Nasan Maimon. Hilkhos Netilas Yadayim LiSeudah 6 is based on 2Likutey Moharan 7 . 00:00 - This shiur is dedicated l'ilui nishmas (for the elevation of the soul) of Rabbi Ozer b'Reb Alexander HaKohen Berger zal , whose 14th yahrzeit was on the day this shiur was given: the 17th of Cheshvan 5781. 01:31 - PARAGRAPH 84. Parshas Ekev and Parshas VaEschanan . 09:06 - Moshe Rabbeinu's defeat of Sichon and Og and the klipos empowering them. 14:44 - Could there be any enemy worse than Haman ? Yes - the klipa personified by Zeresh (wife of Haman ) causes a Jew to fear keeping the Torah. 17:34 - Gesher tzar meod - "The world is a narrow bridge." The message to Yehoshuah was, "Don't be afraid because HaShem is going to defend you." 20:34 - Yehoshuah is the level of student, so he was given the encouragement not to be afraid. His name is composed from the roshei teivos (initial letters) of the verse: Ye kumun Ve Yerannanu SH ochnei Ah for "Rise up and rejoice, those who dwell in dust" ( Yeshayahu 25:19). 25:59 - * Parshas Devarim and Parshas VaEschanan : The greatness of HaShem is revealed through man, because the angels are not as powerful as the tzaddikim of of this world. 28:10 - Q&R about being afraid. A Jew is not permitted to put himself in danger. Tefilas HaDerech - prayer for traveling. Times when fear is appropriate: respect for one's parents, respect for the holiness of a holy place. 30:32 - Q&R what's the difference between "yirah" (awe/respect) and "pachad" (fear of punishment). 32:21 - Q&R about Moshe Rabbeinu's defeat of Sichon and Og . RESPONSE: the klipos (opposing forces) that gave them strength are still operating in our world. 33:45 - * Parshas VaEschanan (continued). The tzaddik "rules over" HaShem . The word "tziyon" sometimes means gravesite, sometimes Eretz Yisrael , and sometimes the tzaddik . Moshe Rabbeinu' s plea to enter Eretz Yisrael because this is the place where the upper and lower worlds can be unified. 36:57 - Man was created by HaShem to be a "partner" in the creation, so man has creative powers that are greater than those of the angels. 38:59 - Why Moshe Rabbeinu pleaded to enter Eretz Yisrael. 43:15 - Joining upper and lower worlds is done through the revelation of Matan Torah . 46:02 - * Chiddush on VaEschanan heard from Rabbi Rosenfeld zal . Reference to the Megalah Amukos . What happened to all of those 515 tefilos poured out by Moshe Rabbeinu ? (515 is the gematria of "TeFiLaH" ). Rebbe Nachman ben Feiga is b'gematria 516. 52:53 - *No tefilah is ever lost. 54:32 - Q&R about the passing of a tzaddik . 59:47 - *Closing blessings. The greatest revelation of HaShem takes place in this world, the lowest one. Current events in light of Torah and tefilah and mitzvos . 61:06 - *Every geulah (redemption) is named after the tzaddik of its time. The word "gam" (also) hints at the Shekhina ( HaShem's Divine Presence in the lower worlds).

lessons.bodyText: Umanin 4 - Parshas Mishpatim - Sukkos - Sukkah - Skhakh - Waving the Arbaah Minim - 4 Species - Speaker: Rabbi Nasan Maimon. 00:00 - PARAGRAPH 14b. - Inner dimensions of Sukkos . 02:30 - Holy desires generate good souls, which promotes life, health and parnassah . 06:15 - The Sukkah is the "Embrace of HaShem" and is associated with Avraham Avinu , holy desires, the Clouds of Glory, and Lechem HaPanim . 09:00 - During Sukkos, 70 korbonos are offered in the Beis Hamikdash , corresponding to the 70 Nations. These offerings pave the way to the ultimate establishment Sukkas Shalom - universal peace. 11:45 - Am Yisrael is destined to become humanity's spiritual leader, as inוְעָמְדוּ זָרִים וְרָעוּ צֹאנְכֶם וּבְנֵי נֵכָר אִכָּרֵיכֶם וְכֹרְמֵיכֶם - "And strangers shall stand and pasture your sheep, and foreigners shall be your plowmen and your vinedressers" ( Yeshaya 61:5). 13:10 - PARAGRAPH 15. Parnassah is related to Sukkos . The sukkah is the bridge between home and field. 17:13 - Parshas Mishpatim. Sukkas is the holiday of harvesting/ingathering, as in וְחַג הָאָסִף בְּצֵאת הַשָּׁנָה בְּאָסְפְּךָ אֶת־מַעֲשֶׂיךָ מִן־הַשָּׂדֶה - "...and the festival of the ingathering at the departure of the year, when you gather in your labors from the field" ( Shemos 23:16, Mishpatim ). 21:00 Reference to Likutey Moharan 48 . 21:15 - PARAGRAPH 16. The spiritual meanings of the Skhakh - the covering of the Sukkah creates shade but doesn't prevent air or vision. 27:00 - The sukkah is like a mother who hovers protectively over her children. 31:40 - PARAGRAPH 17. The Arbaah Minim - the Four Species - correspond to the "4 Who Entered Pardes " and the 4 spiritual levels of Am Yisrael . 29:00 - Q&R about the dual nature of Am Yisrael's relationship with the 70 Nations. 39:00 - Arbaah Minim. Hishtapkhus HaNefesh - Outpouring of the Soul. 42:20 - PARAGRAPH 18. Spiritual dimensions of waving the Arbaah Minim in the 6 Directions. The movements done through waving the 4 Species dispels Unholy Air while the openings in the Sukkah roof allow the influx of Holy Air. This is why the waving of the Arbaah Minim is done in the Sukkah , as brought by the Arizal . 53:00 - Shemini Atzeres .

lessons.bodyText: Sokher 2 - Parshas Pinchas - Health Course - Inner Peace - Universal Peace - Speaker: Rabbi Nasan Maimon. Hilkhos Sokheyr 2 is based on Likutey Moharan 14 . 00:00 - PARAGRAPH 4. The difference between someone who borrows an item vs. a shomer - caretaker. Universal peace depends on bitul - self nullification of physical needs. Universal Peace is brought about through tefilah . HaShem is called "Peace", as in וַיִּקְרָא־לוֹ יְהוָה שָׁלוֹם - "...and he called it HaShem Shalom..." ( Shoftim 6:24). 06:30 - When spiritual needs are given priority, peace is established between body and soul. A person who accomplishes this brings peace to all the worlds. 07:45 - The body is an aspect of tzimtzum - constriction - of spiritual light. 8:40 - Introduction to the concept of putting physical needs above spiritual needs creates an inner state of makhlokes - conflict - in a person. When spiritual needs are given priority over physical demands, peace is established between body and soul. A person who accomplishes this brings peace to all the worlds. 09:30 - NOTE on Moshe Rabbeinu at the sneh - the burning thorn - and the meaning of removing the shoes. 11:30 - Even concerning peace between people, the two aspects of Inner Peace and Universal Peace apply. 13:00 - ***Health Course. Putting physical needs above spiritual needs creates an inner state of makhlokes . When spiritual needs are given priority over physical demands, peace can be established between body and soul, as well as between people. 16:00 - It's important to pray for physical needs. Even so, a person who diminishes or even nullifies physical needs for spiritual reasons can bring about Universal Peace. 20:00 - NOTE about Rabbi Yechiel Michel Dorfman zal - applying this principle to tefilah . 25:00 - Tzedakah . "Increase charity, increase peace" ( Pirkei Avos ). 26:25 - Q&R about tzedakah . Heard from Rabbi Rosenfeld zal quoting the Baal HaTanya zal : when someone has an emergency health issue, increasing tzedakah above the norm can help. 29:55 - Q&R about sanctity even in physical matters that are permissible. 31:15 - How the principles of peace apply to the difference between someone who borrows an item vs. a shomer. 33:20 - *** Prince and Servant - Study Guide - טוֹב־יְהוָה לַכֹּל וְרַחֲמָיו עַל־כָּל־מַעֲשָׂיו "HaShem is good to all, and His mercies are upon all His works" ( Tehillim 145:9). This possuk refers to "when even the animals show mercy to one another". 36:00 - NOTE: When Rebbe Nachman was asked which way to face for tefilah when traveling, he quipped: "Face your suitcase"; that is, don't lose yishuv hadaas or supervision of your belongings, because a journey presents the danger of becoming scatter-brained. 37:00 - NOTE: Megilas Esther - Mordechai watched over Esther's peace. 38:30 - Universal peace - Prince and Servant - Study Guide - לֹא־יָרֵעוּ וְלֹא־יַשְׁחִיתוּ בְּכָל־הַר קָדְשִׁי כִּי־מָלְאָה הָאָרֶץ דֵּעָה אֶת־יְהוָה כַּמַּיִם לַיָּם מְכַסִּים - "They shall neither harm nor destroy on all My holy mount, for the land shall be full of knowledge of the Lord as water covers the seabed" ( Yishaya 11:9). When Universal Peace is activated, even the animals will be at peace with one another, as in וְגָר זְאֵב עִם־כֶּבֶשׂ וְנָמֵר עִם־גְּדִי יִרְבָּץ וְעֵגֶל וּכְפִיר וּמְרִיא יַחְדָּו - "And a wolf shall live with a lamb, and a leopard shall lie with a goat kid; and a calf and a fatling together with a lion..." ( Yishaya 11:6). 42:28 - Q&R about dealing with loss and evil in the present physical world. 45:00 - Q&R about borrowing items or taking loans. 45:40 - PARAGRAPH 5. Birkhas Kohanim . The essence of protection results from שלום. 50:00 - Parshas VeZos HaBerakaha . 52:30 - Parshas Pinchas. 53:50 - Closing blessings. Indexing and Notes by S.Y. Wurtzel. Timings approximate.

lessons.bodyText: Sipurey Maasios - Introduction - Rabbi Yechiel Michel Dorfman zal . Recorded in Jerusalem in 1999 (Yiddish). Translation: "I would like to speak briefly about the about the Rebbe's Sipurey Maasios . Concerning the last story, of 'The Seven Beggars', the Rebbe said: 'If the only reason I came into this world was to tell this one story, it would be enough'. Because in this story the Rebbe there is so much encouragement, so much inspiration, and such refreshment for anyone who wants to renew himself. Because this is certain: an old thing is not good. If an article of clothing is worn even just one time, when it's resold it's worth only half the price. The world likes 'new'. An old man? It's not worth it. The Rebbe didn't like people to be 'old'. The Rebbe said: 'I am very very old and very, very young.' For the way of Breslov, the way of the Rebbe, is that everyday a person should renew himself. Every day he should be a new person, exactly as if he's newborn. And in every story - not just the story of the Seven Beggars, but in every story by the Rebbe a person can derive so much encouragement, so much inspiration and renewal that throughout his entire life he can be renewed. He won't grow older, he'll grow younger." Recording and English Translation by S.Y. Wurtzel.

Hilkhos Genevyva 2 is based on Likutey M
lessons.bodyText: Geneyva 2 - Parshas Bereishis - Parshas Reeh - Parnassah Course - Kabbalah Course - Hashgacha - Left and Right in Kabbalah - Taavas Mamon - Hishtalshelus - How Blessing Flows into the World - Daas - 70 Screams - 140 Screams - Birth Process - Wealth - Speaker: Rabbi Nasan Maimon. Hilkhos Genevyva 2 is based on Likutey Moharan 23 - the debate between Rabbi Yehoshuah ben Chananya and the wise men of Athens. 00:00 - INTRODUCTION. Hashgacha - HaShem's direct supervision. 05:30 - PARAGRAPH 1. PARNASSAH COURSE . Parshas Bereishis . בְּעִצָּבוֹן֙ תֹּֽאכֲלֶ֔נָּה כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י חַיֶּֽיךָ - "...with toil shall you eat of it all the days of your life" ( Bereishis 3:17, Bereishis ). 10:00 - Taavas Mamon : When a person falls into excess desire for money, the Shekhina HaKedosha screams 140 times. 11:30 - Joy is the "light of the face." 11:45 - PARAGRAPH 2. All flow of blessing emanates from דעת ( Nedarim 41). וּבְדַעַת חֲדָרִ֣ים יִמָּלְא֑וּ "With דעת rooms will be filled..." ( Mishlei 24:4). 13:30 - אֹ֣רֶךְ יָ֖מִים בִּֽימִינָ֑הּ בִּ֜שְׂמֹאולָ֗הּ ע֣שֶׁר וְכָבֽוֹד - "Length of days is in its right hand; in its left hand are riches and honor" ( Mishlei 3:16). מִצָּפוֹן זָהָ֣ב יֶֽאֱתֶ֑ה - "Gold originates in the north ..." ( Iyov 37:22). 14:10 - זֹ֚את הַתּוֹרָ֔ה אָדָ֖ם - "This is the Torah - man" ( Bamidbar 19:14, Chukas ). 15:30 - Twice עין is 250. 18:00 - Reference to Likutey Moharan 36 . The Torah was given via the Right Side. 22:00 - Parshas Reeh. וּבֵֽרַכְךָ֙ יְהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ בְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּֽעֲשֶֽׂה - ( Parshas Devarim 15:18, Reeh ). Wealth is an aspect of the Left Side. 24:00 - Arichas Yomim - "Long life" is associated with דעת. 25:40 - Q&R about "The more דעת the more pain." 27:10 - PARAGRAPH 3. Achieving one's livelihood is twice as difficult as giving birth. 30:40 - All blessing, including wealth, is sent to the world via 2 phases. These dual processes relate to the 2 eyes, and the concept of "Left" and "Right". Reference to Likutey Moharan 49 . 32:30 - "Children, life, and livelihood do not depend on מזל." The term מזל refers to the higher realm of כתר where there is no concept of "Left" and "Right". This is the original source from which blessing flows into the lower realms via the lower 7 sefiros where the concept of "Left" and "Right" does pertain. 35:50 - Our 70 screams relate to the first conduit of wealth, the "Left Side". This accomplishes the spiritual transformation of "blood" to "milk" ( Bechoros 6). 38:20 - KABBALAH COURSE. In Arikh Anpin all is רחמים and there is no aspect of "Right" or "Left". 39:30 - Through our first 70 screams we allow the blessing to be released from Arikh Anpin . Through our second 70 screams, we facilitate the blessing's passage through the lower sefiros of Zer Anpin into the physical world. 43:40 - PARAGRAPH 4. Our 140 screams are our best weapon against negative forces opposing the השתלשלות - hishtalshelus (flow of blessing into the physical world through spiritual channels) - first from "Right/Right" and then through "Left/Right". This is why bringing parnassah into the world is twice as difficult as giving birth. 45:45 - Q&R about דעת in daily interactions. Reference to the tefilos following each of the 7 Hakafos of Simchas Torah . Bnei Yissachar : being able to perceive the Torah is a level higher than that of Eliyahu HaNavi . 50:00 - *Q&R - whenever relating to people who don't seem to have דעת: increase one's own humility. 52:30 - *Q&R about the practical application of 70 screams. Reference to Tehillim 20 which has 70 words and to Tehillim 100, which Rebbe Nachman recommends as the perek for giving birth. 54:00 - Closing blessings. Indexing and Notes by S.Y. Wurtzel. Timings approximate.

collections.title: Likutey Halakhos
collections.description: Likutey Halakhos is a commentary on the Shulchan Arukh (Code of Torah Law) in light of the teachings of Rebbe Nachman of Breslov. It was written by Rebbe Nachman's leading student, Rav Nasan of Nemirov. Shiurim covering the eight-volume series were presented by Rabbi Nasan Maimon.

collections.title: Breslov Torah for Women
collections.description: Welcome! Here we'll be linking you to Breslov teachings especially relevant to women. A true, contemporary story about faith and fulfillment can really light up the soul. We look forward to sharing many! Here's one told by R' Nasan Maimon about a family in our community: A Woman's Tears LM2 - Torah 24 - Mitzvah Gedolah - Part 1 of 2 - Rabbi Nasan Maimon LM2 - Torah 24 - Mitzvah Gedolah - Part 2 of 2 - Rabbi Nasan Maimon Living Breslov Chassidus at home: VaYechi - Women and the Geulah (Clip) And in the heart: Rabbi Zvi Aryeh Rosenfeld z"l on Tznius /Modesty and Hair Covering Having Faith in Oneself - Sichos HaRan - Paragraph 140 Raising Hashem's Children: Why are Tzitzis a Boy's First Mitzvah ? (Clip) Keeping Kosher: Tevilas Keilim (Mikveh Immersion of Dining and Food Preparation Utensils) - GUIDELINES What is Tikkun HaBris (Guarding the Covenant) for Women? Speaker: Rabbi Nasan Maimon. The teaching " Mitzvah gedolah l'hiyos b'simcha tamid – it's a fundamental Torah commandment to be happy always" ( Likutey Moharan II, 24) reveals the relationship between physical and spiritual health: Likutey Moharan 2, Torah 24 - Joy, the Ten Pulses, and the Ten Types of Song in Sefer Tehillim Speaker: Sara Wurtzel

collections.title: R' Rosenfeld - Likutey Moharan 1
collections.description: The Likutey Moharan translated into English and explained by רבי צבי ארי-ה בן ציון רוזנפלד ז"ל - Rabbi Zvi Aryeh Rosenfeld zal . He began recording this series in Shevat 5720 (February, 1960) and completed it Ohr l' 26 Kislev 5721 (1960-12-14).

collections.title: Likutey Moharan 2
collections.description: Rebbe Nachman introduced Part 2 of the Likutey Moharan in the summer of 1808 after teaching the lesson " Ayeh " (LM2 - Torah 12). It was compiled by Rav Nosson of Nemirov and first published in 1811, during the year after Rebbe Nachman's passing ( Yemey Moharnat I, #29; Sichos HaRan #144). The text is read, translated into English, and explained by Rabbi Nasan Maimon.

collections.title: Aitzos HaMevuoros - Faith
collections.description: Aitzos HaMevuoros – Advice Clarified – was written by a great-grandson of Rebbe Nachman of Breslov, Rabbi Shimshon Barsky. It's a treasury of practical guidance about the basics of emunah (Jewish faith in Hashem and in His Torah) and how to implement Breslov chassidus into daily life. This series of five lectures was given by Rabbi Nasan Maimon in Jerusalem beginning on Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5775 (2015-04-20).

collections.title: Azamra - The Good Point
collections.description: " Azamra "(I will sing) is the name of Likutey Moharan Torah 282 -- one of Rebbe Nachman's most fundamental teachings. It's about finding the "good point" in others, and in ourselves. Appreciating our own unique abilities to be aware of Hashem helps us serve Him with joy, day by day.

collections.title: Hishtapkhus - Outpouring of the Soul
collections.description: Hishtapkhus HaNefesh (Outpouring of the Soul) is a collection of Rabbi Nachman's teachings about Hisbodedus - literally "seclusion" - voluntary prayer in one's own words in addition to strengthen, enrich, and empower the individual's emotional connection to the traditional mandatory prayers from the siddur (Jewish prayer book). The text is translated into and explained in English by Rabbi Nasan Maimon. The sefer was compiled by Rabbi Moshe Yehoshua Bezhilianski (known as Reb Alter of Teplik) and first published in Jerusalem about 1904. Reb Alter was born in Teplik, Ukraine, and was the son-in-law of one of Rav Nosson of Nemirov's closest students, Reb Nachman Chazan. He became a leading teacher of Breslov chassidus throughout Europe and Russia by writing, publishing, and distributing a number of works about the teachings of Rabbi Nachman. In the words of Rabbi Aryeh Kaplan z"l : " provides a path through which even the most unlearned Jew can find his way back to God."

collections.title: Simcha - Joy
collections.description: Welcome to a journey that will transform your life for the better! True and lasting happiness is not a mood that can be affected by events, relationships, or material possessions. It's an ongoing series of quiet accomplishments that only you and Hashem can see. Rebbe Nachman of Breslov taught: "It's a great mitzvah to always be happy..." ( Likutey Moharan 2:24). The question is: how? Rabbi Maimon has culled from a number of Breslov sources to guide you on the path that doesn't simply lead you to some distant, better place. The path itself is that better place!

collections.title: Sipurey Masiyos - The 13 Stories
collections.description: This series of lectures presents the Sipurey Masiyos ( The 13 Stories ) of Rebbe Nachman of Breslov as explained in English by Rabbi Nasan Maimon. Characters personify qualities within every Jewish soul. These mystical allegories contain some of the Torah's deepest secrets and were originally published in Yiddish so women and children could enjoy and benefit from them.

collections.title: R' Rosenfeld - Praises of Rebbe Nachman
collections.description: Shevachey HaRan – Praises of Rebbe Nachman – is a biography written by the chassidic master's closest student: Rav Nosson of Nemirov zal . In his introduction to this sefer Rav Nosson writes: "Presented here is less than a drop in the ocean of the Rebbe's profound holiness and greatness.... Rather than publicize our teacher's miracles and wondrous deeds, our main goal is to provide concepts that will bring others closer to HaShem . May those who read this find a way." The Hebrew text is translated into English and explained by Rabbi Zvi Aryeh Rosenfeld zal .

collections.title: R' Rosenfeld - Sichos HaRan by Lesson
collections.description: Sichos HaRan - Wise Sayings of Rebbe Nachman - is the spiritual legacy of Rebbe Nachman of Breslov's teachings that was entrusted to his students in conversations. Written and arranged by Rav Noson Sternhartz zal , it's here translated into English and explained by Rabbi Zvi Aryeh Rosenfeld zal in a series of recordings made from September 1975 until 1978, the year of his passing.
collections.hebrewTranslation: שיחות הר"ן - רבי צבי אריה רוזנפלד ז"ל

collections.title: Ein Yaakov
collections.description: Ein Yaakov is a collection of the Aggadah of the Talmud. It was compiled by Rabbi Yaakov ibn Habib and – after his passing – by his son Rabbi Levi ibn Habib. It is presented here by רבי צבי ארי-ה רוזנפלד ז"ל Rabbi Zvi Aryeh Ben-Zion Rosenfeld zal , a revered Breslov scholar who shared his mastery of Ein Yaakov with students in a way that transformed their lives. B"H Rabbi Rosenfeld had the foresight to record these shiurim , entrusting the hidden wisdom of Ein Yaakov to future generations. Rabbi Moshe Chaim Luzzatto zal explains that Aggadah are multi-layered commentaries on the Torah. Each narrative has literal meanings (חלק המצוות) and allegorical (חלק הסודות) or "secret" meanings. The "secret" components contain aspects of the Talmud so powerful that the rabbis of the Mishnaic era "encoded" their messages as "stories" to prevent their power from being misused. Rabbi Rosenfeld presents the keys to understanding Ein Yaakov in ways that enable listeners to unlock the doors of their true potential.

collections.title: NaCh - Prophets and Writings
collections.description: This is a series of lectures on the history of the People of Israel based on NaCh ( Nevi'im /Prophets and C'suvim /Writings). It's presented by Rabbi Zvi Aryeh Rosenfeld z”l , an accomplished and revered Torah scholar who spearheaded the introduction of Breslov chassidus to the English-speaking world.

pages.title: Breslov Topics
pages.bodyText: Pictured above is the " Alta Heim " that sheltered all who came to pray at the gravesite of Rebbe Nachman of Breslov from shortly after his passing until its destruction during World War 2. Quick inspiration from Breslov chassidus about... ASHREY - this Hebrew word for "fortunate" or "accomplished" appears in Sefer Tehillim 22 times - why? When we say the familiar verses of Dovid HaMelech three times a day, what does this establish? BEIS HAMIKDASH – Jerusalem's once and future temple will be a house of prayer for all nations and will stand forever because it's being built from our tefilos (prayers). BLESSINGS – Saying, hearing, and answering " omen " to brochos (blessings) on food nourishes the soul and strengthens physical health, too. Why are there no blessings to say after enjoying fragrance as there are after enjoying food? BRIS MILAH – What are the deeper meanings of the mitzvah of Bris Milah (circumcision)? How does Tikkun haBris (moral restraint) empower and protect the individual and the community? BUSINESS – The kabbalah of fair trade is based on some of the deepest secrets in the Torah. Success in business is a result of honesty and faith in Hashem. CASH FLOW is increased through netilas yadayim (washing hands before eating bread). CHARITY – Tzadakah : how does it empower the one who gives? CHILDREN – What is naches ? Praying for that first child and raising children to care. Should young children be brought to shul (synagogue)? DEPRESSION – Feeling emotionally or spiritually paralyzed is a form of sleep. Rebbe Nachman's advice for waking up from despair. Praying when you feel down. ERETZ YISRAEL – Developing our appreciation of and spiritual connection to the Holy Land of Israel – past, present, and future. EDUCATION – The importance of limud Torah, as an individual and as family. FAITH – Nurturing emunah (Jewish faith) even through times of adversity. Believing that even the slightest thought, word, or act of returning to HaShem has tremendous significance. FOOD FOR THE SOUL - Enjoying the spiritual aspects of eating and drinking in a kosher, self-respecting way. HEALTH – Understanding and coping with illness. Breslov chassidus brings resources on how to value and care for physical and emotional well-being. When a person is ill, why do we use the mother's name when praying for their recovery ? HOLIDAYS – Timely lectures about the upcoming yomim tovim . HOLY PLACES – Information about how to visit Kivrei Tzadikim , including maps and a photo gallery. JOY – Converting temporary celebrations into simcha (lasting happiness). Rebbe Nachman taught practical techniques for weathering challenges with calm, clear serenity. KASHRUS – Guidelines for tevilas keilim ( mikveh immersion of cooking and dining utensils) . KAVANA (Intent) in Prayer. Dealing with the reality of wavering concentration. How is it that a tzaddik 's prayer can be more powerful than that of even many people? MARRIAGE – Secrets for maintaining peace and prosperity in the home. The relationship between husband and wife needs tending . Rabbi Rosenfeld z"l explores: why is the path to marriage so difficult? MAZAL – What is it? How can we change it? MIDOS – Perfection is a heavenly, not a human attribute. Self mastery can be achieved with the help of chassidic techniques of bitul (temporary suspension of self) and rotzo v’shov (“running and returning”) . Developing courage through greater self-knowledge and compassion. MITZVOS - Making a mitzvah beautiful - why and how? MODESTY - Tzniyus (restraint in speech, behavior, and clothing) brings blessing to the individual and protection to the People of Israel. MONEY – What promotes parnassa (income) and facilitates sustainable cash-flow for shalom bayis ? Working and learning Torah - achieving a balance. MOURNING – Halachos and minhagim (laws and customs) of loss; the deeper meanings of shiva , aveylus , and yahrzeits . The deep meaning of saying Kaddish for a parent. MUSIC – Even humming a tune quietly can refresh your soul. Hold onto the invincible power of song. Rav Nossan of Nemirov advised his students to “Dance every day.” Rabbi Zvi Aryeh Rosenfeld singing the Rebbe's Nigun , according to the traditional cadence received from his teacher, the leading Breslov elder of his previous generation, Rabbi Avraham Sternhartz zal . PAIN – What purpose does it serve? How can it be dealt with on a spiritual level? Transforming the stress of emotional or physical suffering into positive energy toward recovery with Hashem's help. PARANORMAL – Demons? Ghosts? Monsters? Extraterrestrials? They're all mentioned in the Talmud and some are even described in detail. Fasten your seat belts. PATIENCE – Arichas Apayim is acquired through humility, the key to all character refinement. Breathing deeply and holding silent when anger flares up enable a person to think clearly before speaking or taking action. PRAYER – The role of the tzaddikim in the generation. Achieving power and concentration during tefilah and speaking to Hashem in your own words ( hisbodedus ). Praying when you feel down. RABBI – Why it's important to give the name of someone who is ill to one's rabbi for tefilah . Finding the best Torah mentor for who you are. Emunas chochomim (faith in one’s Rabbi) is the secret to spiritual success. ROSH CHODESH – The deeper meanings of the months of the lunar calendar, month by month . SELF-ESTEEM – Confidence in yourself and true humility are really the same thing. Appreciating and activating your infinite potential is a crucial element in emunah (faith). SHABBOS – Making this week's Shabbos the best ever. When do we receive our Neshoma Yiseyra (Additional Shabbos Soul)? SHALOM BAYIS – A peaceful home depends on understanding the deeper aspects of the relationship between husband and wife. SOUL MATE – Finding and appreciating your z ivug (marriage partner). How to retain those special feelings of connection through life's challenges. SPEECH – How it affects our soul and our world. How Viduy (confession) releases impurities that limit us. TEHILLIM helps a person return to Hashem and His Torah. TIKKUN HABRIS Is Tikkun Cheyt Adam HaRishon and Chava . TIKKUN HABRIS - an overview through Jewish history - achieving tikkun habris through following the advice of the tzaddik. TIKKUN HAKLALI – The 10 Psalms revealed by Rebbe Nachman as the "General Remedy" for spiritual recovery. ( Tehillim /Psalms 16, 32, 41, 42, 59, 77, 90, 105, 137, and 150.) TODAY – Free yourself from dwelling on past or future and make the most of the present. TORAH STUDY – Rebbe Nachman’s advice is to study consistently and quickly. He encourages that a little bit every day is infinitely better than nothing. TZITZIS - Why are they a young boy's first mitzvah ? UMAN – Its meaning in Breslov chassidus , history , and current events. WILL POWER – Getting free of an addiction? Losing weight? Determined to stay within your budget? Tap into your reservoirs of spiritual strength for results that last. If YIDDISH speaks to your heart, we hope you enjoy a new series by Reb Yechiel Michel Dorfman z"l on the Stories of Rebbe Nachman. YIRAS HaSHEM - respect for HaShem - is the foundation of all Torah wisdom and practice.

pages.title: About Us
pages.bodyText: Rabbi Nasan Maimon Rabbi Maimon received smicha (rabbinic ordination) from the Central Yeshiva of Chassidei Breslov in Meah Shaarim, Jerusalem. Originally from New York City, he was a close student of Rabbi Tzvi Aryeh Rosenfeld zal and eventually became his son-in-law. He was appointed Executive Director of the Breslov World Center in 1978 and has headed the Breslov Yeshiva's English-speaking kollel since making aliyah to Jerusalem in 1987. In 2008 he established as an online resource center for students of Rebbe Nachman all over the world. Fluent in English, Yiddish and Hebrew, Rabbi Maimon translates and explains original texts in a practical, straightforward way. His knowledge is informed by decades of close apprenticeship to his teachers, Rabbi Rosenfeld and Rabbi Yechiel Michel Dorfman zal . After Rabbi Dorfman's passing in 2006, Rabbi Maimon consulted Rabbis Moshe and Nachman Burstein zal . Rabbi Maimon is recognized internationally as a dynamic teacher, compassionate listener, and experienced counselor who provides well-grounded application of the teachings of Rebbe Nachman to contemporary life. Rabbi Tzvi Aryeh Rosenfeld zal Rabbi Zvi Aryeh b'Reb Yisrael Abba Rosenfeld (1922- 11th Kislev 5739/1978) was an accomplished and universally respected Torah scholar who shared his knowledge with students in ways that uplifted and transformed their lives. With tremendous self-sacrifice and dedication, he introduced Breslov Chassidus to the English-speaking world. In 1945 he received smicha (rabbinical ordination) from Rav Avraham Yoffen zal , Rosh of the Beis Yosef Navardak Yeshiva, and in 1949 he received additional ordination from Rav Avrohom Sternhartz zal , recognized leader of Breslover Chassidus in Ukraine and Yerushalayim. Rabbi Rosenfeld is a direct descendant of Rav Aharon Goldstein zal , the Rav of Breslov during the lifetime of Rebbe Nachman and one of the Rebbe's closest students. He is also a descendant of Rabbi Shmuel Yitzchak zal , Rav of Tcherin. Rabbi Rosenfeld had the foresight to record hundreds of his shiurim , entrusting them to future generations as vital keys to the powerful wisdom of Rebbe Nachman of Breslov. Rabbi Yechiel Michel Dorfman zal "Reb Michel" (as Rabbi Dorfman was known) (Ukraine 1913-Yerushalayim Ihr HaKodesh, 2006) was a devoted and much-beloved elder in the Breslov community worldwide. His father, HaRav Yehoshua Dovid HaLevi, may his blood be avenged, was a leading Rabbi in the city of Chemirovitz, Kaminetz-Podolsk until he was murdered by the Nazis in August, 1941. Rabbi Dorfman was drawn to Breslov chas s idus shortly after he became bar mitzvah and studied closely with the leaders of the previous generation. When he was 16 years old, his teacher, Rav Avrohom Sternhartz zal , suggested his granddaughter, Rivkah (bas Mariasa Shochet and R' Nosson Sternhartz) as a wife. The couple married in Shevat , 1930, and as newlyweds lived in a room in Rav Avrohom's home in Breslov. Surviving extreme hardships in communist Russia, the Dorfmans raised a Torah-observant family and maintained unfailing trust in HaShem. Even when Reb Michel was imprisoned in Siberia he never lost hope. For 38 years he and his wife were forbidden to leave Russia until finally, in 1971, they were granted exit visas and flew straight to Eretz Yisrael. In addition to heading the Breslov Kollel in Meah She’arim from 1979, in 1989 Rabbi Levi Yitzchok Bender zal appointed Rabbi Dorfman as his successor to co-direct the Central Breslov Yeshiva in Meah She’arim. Tirelessly, Reb Michel rose every night to pray at Chatzos (midnight), immerse in the mikveh , and began his day. He davened , taught, counseled, raised funds for the yeshiva, organized the yearly Rosh Hashanah kibbutz (gathering) in Uman, supervised the construction of the Breslov synagogue and 5 mikvaos in Uman, and faithfully led the daily Netz Minyan, (prayer at daybreak) 7 days a week, until his passing on the 5th of Av ( Yahrzeit of the ARIzal ) at the age of 93. Through tefilos, tears, and monumental self-sacrifice, Reb Michel Dorfman was a spiritual guide for countless families and paved the way for the Rosh Hashanah gathering in Uman to reach its present dimensions. His Kever is on Har HaZeisim among the elders of Breslov. Breslov Torah - Activities and Goals With gratitude to Hashem, through support of donors and students, Rabbi Nasan Maimon and his team are: Teaching Breslov chassidus via the internet Enabling the Torah study of future Breslov teachers Lecturing in Breslov chassidus worldwide Counseling individuals and families Establishing special prayers and memorial services at holy sites in Eretz Yisrael and in Uman Supporting and participating in the life-cycle events of students and their families Breslov Torah Affiliates Ohr haNe'elam is a full-time kollel of 100 students and their families in Jerusalem. Founded by Rabbi Rosenfeld and expanded by Reb Michel Dorfman, its participants study of Gemara, Halacha , and Chassidus . Kollel Chatzos shel Breslov baKosel , a pre-dawn Kollel at the Kosel haMa'aravi , offers donors participation in Torah study and tefilos ( prayers). Reb Michel Dorfman and Rabbi Nasan Maimon at the gravesite of Reb Noson of Nemirov, Breslov, 2004. Rescuing Rebbe Nachman's Gravesite in Uman In 1979 the Soviets planned to destroy Rabbi Nachman’s grave in Uman to make way for a housing project. The leaders of the international Breslov community appointed Rabbi Michel Dorfman ז"ל as their spokesman to avert this threat. Reb Michel first went straight to the kosel where he begged, with heartfelt tears and prayers, for Divine intervention. Then, although he spoke no English, Reb Michel immediately traveled to the U.S. where Rabbi Nasan Maimon served as his translator and close assistant. Together they solicited and received endorsements from HaRav Moshe Feinstein זצ"ל and other gedolei Torah. The Satmar Rebbe, Lubavitcher Rebbe, Rav Moshe Sherer, Rav Pinchas Teitz, and Rabbi Aryeh Kaplan all supported and contributed their wisdom and guidance to the mission. With their help, Rabbi Maimon and Reb Michel zal were able to present the Jewish community's petition to officials from the U.S. State Department and the Kremlin. B"H the petition succeeded and the gravesite of Rebbe Nachman was preserved. This miracle also protected the nearby mass grave of some 30,000 Jewish martyrs of the Chmielnitsky massacres. As a direct result of these efforts blessed with success by Hashem , hundreds of thousands have been able to visit this holy site since that time.

pages.title: Our Mission
pages.bodyText: Every day, more and more people from all walks of life are turning to the teachings of Rebbe Nachman of Breslov for inspiration and practical guidance to aid their spiritual growth and fulfillment. Breslov Torah’s MISSION is to make the treasury of Rebbe Nachman’s wisdom accessible to all and help apply it to our daily lives. We aim to enrich Jewish communities and individuals with inspirational and transformative EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES as well as to provide SOCIAL SERVICES to families and people in need. About Us Breslov Torah is led by Rabbi Nasan Maimon who is internationally recognized as a dynamic teacher, compassionate listener, and experienced counselor who provides well-grounded applications of Rebbe Nachman’s teachings to contemporary life. Rabbi Nasan Maimon provides education and counseling to English speaking communities worldwide. His classes as well as the teachings of his Rabbi and mentor, Rabbi Tzvi Areyh Rosenfeld z”l are disseminated via our website BreslovTorah.com. Our Website The website houses the internet’s largest searchable database in the teachings of Rebbi Nachman and serves as a reliable source for English speakers seeking to connect with Breslov chassidus. Its media library contains over 4000 authoritative, text-based shiurim (Torah lectures) and serves as a worldwide hub for a vital, expanding community of students and their families. Breslov Kollels In addition to servicing Anglo-communities, Breslov Torah maintains several traditional Breslov kollels (study groups) which house over 100 scholars. These kollels are an integral part of developing future Breslov teachers and leaders as well as sustaining the link/messorah between the original chassidim of Rebbe Nachman and the aspiring students of today. Ohr haNe’elam is a full-time kollel founded by Rabbi Rosenfeld and expanded by Rabbi Michel Dorfman and is situated in the Breslov Shul of Meah Shearim, Jerusalem. Kollel Chatzos shel Breslov baKosel is a pre-dawn kollel at the Western Wall and offers donors the opportunity to dedicate Torah study and request special prayers at this most auspicious time and location. Breslov Torah also promotes Rebbe Nachman’s integral practice of hitbodedut (secluded personal prayer and meditation) by sponsoring a nightly bus shuttle providing free transportation from the Breslov Shul to the peaceful fields of Jerusalem. Assisting Those in Need In tandem with our educational mission, Breslov Torah is also dedicated to assisting individuals and families in need. Rabbi Nasan Maimon is often approached by many sincere people who cannot supply their families with even the most basic requirements such as food, shelter and clothing. In addition, while some struggling families manage to get by with the most minimum of needs, they are desperate for assistance when it comes to organizing special occasions such as weddings and Bar Mitzvahs. As such, Rabbi Nasan Maimon distributes life-saving tzedakah and serves as a vital link between those with the ability to give and those in need. Future Goals To open a Breslov Torah Center for the Anglo-sector where students can attend live shiurim and get practical guidance towards the application of Breslov chassidus into their personal lives. This location will also host special programs and will serve as a community center where students connect with rabbis and each other. Shiurim will be given by Rabbi Maimon and several other rabbis. This center will also function as a training ground to support developing the next generation of Breslov leaders and teachers. To expand the functionality of our website by indexing all of its shiurim. This will increase the site’s “searchability” and make the shiurim more valuable as learning and research resources. To expand the kollel programs. Currently there are about 100 scholars in this program and there is a waiting list to join. To build a hospitality center in Uman to serve the Breslov Torah community. The center will accommodate people with lodging, meals, and a shul/beit midrash for shiurim.

pages.title: Hilkhos Matanos l'Evyonim (Gifts to the Poor) on Purim
pages.bodyText: In response to the miracles performed for Am Yisroel during the events of Purim , Mordechai and Esther introduced the obligation of Matanos l'Evyonim , giving gifts to the poor on Purim . Our sages, based on the plural of “gifts” in the Megillah , established the mitzvah of giving a gift to at least two poor people on Purim ( Megillah 7b, Be’er Heiteiv 694:1). Concerning this mitzvah , the Rambam says: "It is better to provide more gifts to the poor than to have a costlier Purim seudah or to send more shalach manos ( Rambam, Hilkhos Megillah 2:17). Even a poor person who receives charity must give Matanos l'Evyonim ( Bach, Tur on Shulchan Aruch 694). The minimum amounts for this gift vary from “two small coins” to “a respectful amount”, but all Torah authorities agree that one should give the recipients something to benefit their celebration of Purim ( Pri Megadim, Mishbetzos Zahav 694:1). Money for Matanos l'Evyonim can be designated before Purim because if the poor person receives the money on Purim , one fulfills the mitzvah ( Be’er Heiteiv 695:7; Aruch HaShulchan 694:2). A woman is obligated in Matanos l'Evyonim ( Shulchan Aruch 695:4). Although a married woman may be included in the gift given by her husband, the Magen Avraham encourages a married woman to distribute money to the poor herself on Purim . One may not use money collected for Matanos l'Evyonim for a different tzedakah ( Bava Metzia 78b). To designate R' Nasan Maimon to give Matonos L'Evyonim on your behalf this year, please click HERE .

pages.title: Tefilas HaSheLaH HaKadosh - A Parent's Prayer - Erev Rosh Chodesh Sivan
pages.bodyText: אַתָּה הוּא יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא בָרָאתָ הָעוֹלָם, וְאַתָּה הוּא אֱלֹהֵינוּ מִשֶּׁבָּרָאתָ הָעוֹלָם, וּמֵעוֹלָם וְעַד עוֹלָם אַתָּה אֵל, וּבָרָאתָ עוֹלָמְךָ בְּגִין לְאִשְתְּמוֹדַע אֱלָהוּתָךְ בְּאֶמְצָעוּת תּוֹרָתְךָ הַקְּדוֹשָׁה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינּו זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה, בְּרֵאשִׁית – בִּשְׁבִיל תּוֹרָה וּבִשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל, כִּי הֵם עַמְּךָ וְנַחֲלָתְךָ אֲשֶׁר בָּחַרְתָּ בָּהֶם מִכָּל הָאֻמּוֹת, וְנָתַתָּ לָהֶם תּוֹרָתְךָ הַקְּדוֹשָׁה, וְקֵרַבְתָּם לְשִׁמְךָ הַגָּדוֹל וְעַל קִיּוּם הָעוֹלָם וְעַל קִיּוּם הַתּוֹרָה בָּאוּ לָנוּ מִמְּךָ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ שְׁנֵי צִוּוּיִים כָּתַבְתָּ בְּתוֹרָתְךָ פְּרוּ וּרְבוּ, וְכָתַבְתָּ בְּתוֹרָתְךָ וְלִמַּדְתֶּם אֹתָם אֶת בְּנֵיכֶם, וְהַכַּוָּנָה בִשְׁתֵּיהֶן אֶחָת, כִּי לֹא לְתֹהוּ בָרָאתָ כִּי אִם לָשֶׁבֶת, וְלִכְבוֹדְךָ בָּרָאתָ יָצַרְתָּ אַף עָשִׂיתָ, כְּדֵי שֶׁנִּהְיֶה אֲנַחְנוּ וְצֶאֱצָאֵינוּ וְצֶאֱצָאֵי כָּל עַמְּךָ בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל יוֹדְעֵי שְׁמֶךָ וְלוֹמְדֵי תוֹרָתֶךָ וּבְכֵן אָבוֹא אֵלֶיךָ יְיָ מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים, וְאַפִּיל תְּחִנָּתִי, וְעֵינַי לְךָ תְּלוּיוֹת עַד שֶׁתְּחָנֵּנִי וְתִשְׁמַע תְּפִלָּתִי לְהַזְמִין לִי בָּנִים וּבָנוֹת, וְגַם הֵם יִפְרוּ וְיִרְבּוּ הֵם וּבְנֵיהֶם וּבְנֵי בְנֵיהֶם עַד סוֹף כָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת לְתַכְלִית שֶּׁהֵם וַאֲנִי כֻּלָּנוּ יַעַסְקוּ בְּתוֹרָתְךָ הַקְּדוֹשָׁה לִלְמֹד וּלְלַמֵּד לִשְׁמֹר וְלַעֲשׂוֹת וּלְקַיֵּם אֶת כָּל דִּבְרֵי תַלְמוּד תּוֹרָתְךָ בְּאַהֲבָה, וְהָאֵר עֵינֵינוּ בְּתוֹרָתֶךָ וְדַבֵּק לִבֵּנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתֶיךָ לְאַהֲבָה וּלְיִרְאָה אֶת שְׁמֶךָ אָבִינוּ אָב הָרַחֲמָן, תֵּן לְכֻלָּנוּ חַיִּים אֲרוּכִים וּבְרוּכִים, מִי כָמוֹךָ אַב הָרַחֲמִים זוֹכֵר יְצוּרָיו לְחַיִּים בְּרַחֲמִים, זָכְרֵנוּ לְחַיִּים נִצְחִיִּים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁהִתְפַּלֵּל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ לוּ יִחְיֶה לְפָנֶיךָ, וּפֵרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה, בְּיִרְאָתֶךָ כִּי עַל כֵּן בָּאתִי לְבַקֵּשׁ וּלְחַנֵּן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ שֶׁיְּהֵא זַרְעִי וְזֶרַע זַרְעִי עַד עוֹלָם זֶרַע כָּשֵׁר, וְאַל יִמָּצֵא בִי וּבְזַרְעִי וּבְזֶרַע זַרְעִי עַד עוֹלָם שׁוּם פְּסוּל וָשֶׁמֶץ, אַךְ שָׁלוֹם וֶאֱמֶת וְטוֹב וְיָשָׁר בְּעֵינֵי אֱלֹהִים וּבְעֵינֵי אָדָם, וְיִהְיוּ בַּעֲלֵי תוֹרָה, מָארֵי מִקְרָא, מָארֵי מִשְׁנָה, מָארֵי תַלְמוּד, מָארֵי רָזָא, מָארֵי מִצְוָה, מָארֵי גוֹמְלֵי חֲסָדִים, מָארֵי מִדּוֹת תְּרוּמִיּוֹת, וְיַעַבְדּוּךָ בְּאַהֲבָה וּבְיִרְאָה פְּנִימִית, לֹא יִרְאָה חִיצוֹנִית, וְתֵן לְכָל גְּוִיָּה וּגְוִיָּה מֵהֶם דֵּי מַחְסוֹרָה בְּכָבוֹד, וְתֵן לָהֶם בְּרִיאוּת וְכָבוֹד וָכֹחַ, וְתֵן לָהֶם קוֹמָה וְיֹפִי וְחֵן וָחֶסֶד, וְיִהְיֶה אַהֲבָה וְאַחֲוָה וְשָׁלוֹם בֵּינֵיהֶם, וְתַזְמִין לָהֶם זִוּוּגִים הֲגוּנִים מִזֶּרַע תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים מִזֶּרַע צַדִּיקִים, וְגַם זִוּוּגָם יִהְיוּ כְּמוֹתָם כְּכָל אֲשֶׁר הִתְפַּלַּלְתִּי עֲלֵיהֶם, כִּי זִכָּרוֹן אֶחָד עוֹלֶה לְכָאן וּלְכָאן אַתָּה יְיָ יוֹדֵעַ כָּל תַּעֲלוּמוֹת, וּלְפָנֶיךָ נִגְלוּ מַצְפּוּנֵי לִבִּי, כִּי כַוָּנָתִי בְּכָל אֵלֶּה לְמַעַן שִׁמְךָ הַגָּדוֹל וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ וּלְמַעַן תּוֹרָתְךָ הַקְּדוֹשָׁה, עַל כֵּן עֲנֵנִי יְיָ עֲנֵנִי בַּעֲבוֹר הָאָבוֹת הַקְּדוֹשִׁים אַבְרָהָם יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב, וּבִגְלָלָם תּוֹשִׁיעַ בָּנִים לִהְיוֹת הָעֲנָפִים דּוֹמִים לְשָׁרְשָׁם, וּבַעֲבוּר דָוִד עַבְדֶּךָ רֶגֶל רְבִיעִי בַּמֶּרְכָּבָה, הַמְשׁוֹרֵר בְּרוּחַ קָדְשֶׁךָ שִׁיר הַמַּעֲלוֹת, אַשְׁרֵי כָּל יְרֵא יְיָ הַהֹלֵךְ בִּדְרָכָיו: יְגִיעַ כַּפֶּיךָ כִּי תֹאכֵל אַשְׁרֶיךָ וְטוֹב לָךְ אֶשְׁתְּךָ כְּגֶפֶן פֹּרִיָּה בְּיַרְכְּתֵי בֵיתֶךָ, בָּנֶיךָ כִּשְׁתִלֵי זֵיתִים סָבִיב לְשֻׁלְחָנֶךָ הִנֵּה כִּי כֵן יְבֹרַךְ גָּבֶר יְרֵא יְיָ יְבָרֶכְךָ יְיָ מִצִּיּוֹן, וּרְאֵה בְּטוּב יְרוּשָלָיִם, כֹּל יְמֵי חַיֶּיךָ וּרְאֵה בָנִים לְבָנֶיךָ, שָׁלוֹם עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל אָנָּא יְיָ שוֹמֵעַ תְּפִלָּה, יְקֻיַּם בָּנוּ הַפָּסוּק, וַאֲנִי זֹאת בְּרִיתִי אוֹתָם אָמַר יְיָ, רוּחִי אֲשֶׁר עָלֶיךָ וּדְבָרַי אֲשֶׁר שַׂמְתִּי בְּפִיך, לֹא יָמוּשׁוּ מִפִּיךָ וּמִפִּי זַרְעֲךָ וּמִפִּי זֶרַע זַרְעֲךָ אָמַר יְיָ מֵעַתָּה וְעַד עוֹלָם יִהְיוּ לְרָצוֹן אִמְרֵי פִי וְהֶגְיוֹן לִבִּי לְפָנֶיךָ יְיָ צוּרִי וְגֹאֲלִי Hashem, You were Hashem, Elokeinu (Our Master), before You created the world; You have been Hashem, Elokeinu, since You created the world; and from this world to the next, You are Elokeinu. You created Your world to reveal Your Sovereignty through Your holy Torah, as our Sages of blessed memory, teach: “’In the beginning…’ for the sake of Torah and for the sake of Israel…” For Israel is Your Nation and Your heritage, chosen by You from all other nations, to whom You gave Your holy Torah, and brought close to Your great Name. To preserve the continuation of Your Torah, we received from You, Hashem, our G-d, two commandments: "Be fruitful and multiply" (Bereishis 1:28 ) and " You shall teach them to your children" (Devarim 1 1:19 ) . Their purpose is that You did not create the world to be empty, but to be inhabited by people. And it is for Your glory that You created, shaped, and perfected the world, so that we, and our descendants, and all the descendants of Your People, the House of Israel, could know Your Name and study Your Torah. And so I come to You, Hashem, King above All Kings, setting my appeal before You. My eyes turn to You with dependence that You will be gracious and hear my prayer and grant me sons and daughters. And may they, too, be fruitful and multiply – they and their descendants throughout all generations, so that they and we may study Your holy Torah – learning, teaching, safeguarding, performing, and fulfilling with love all the words of Your Torah. Enlighten our eyes in Your Torah and attach our heart to Your commandments to love and revere Your Name. Our Father, compassionate Father, grant us all a long and blessed life. Who is like You, compassionate Father, Who mercifully remembers His creatures for life! Remember us for eternal life, as Avraham our father prayed, "If only Yishmael would live before You," (Bereishis 17:18). For this reason I come to ask and plead before You, that my children and their children be kasher, and that You never find in them a disqualifying blemish or fault. May they have peace, truth, goodness and integrity in the eyes of G-d and man. Help them to become masterful in Torah, accomplished in TeNach, Mishnah, Talmud, Kabbalah, mitzvos, deeds of kindness, and refined character, serving You with a true, inner love and reverence for Heaven, not merely for appearances. Please provide for each of my descendants according to their needs in a respectable way, granting every one of them health, honor, and strength. Give them stature and good appearance, grace, and kindness. May there be love, brotherhood and peace among them. Provide them with suitable marriage partners of scholarly and righteous parentage. And may each of their spouses also be blessed with all that I have asked for my own descendants, since one prayer can affect the lives of many. You, Hashem, know all that’s hidden and before You the secrets of my heart are revealed. May all that I'm asking be for the sake of Your great and holy Name and for the sake of Your holy Torah. Therefore, answer me, Hashem, please answer me in the merit of our holy forefathers Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov, because ancestors help their children, so that the branches will be like the roots. for the sake of Your servant, Dovid, the fourth support of Your Chariot, who sings, by means of Your Divine inspiration: “A Song of Ascents. Fortunate is everyone who fears Hashem, who walks in His ways. When you eat of the toil of your hands, you are fortunate and you will have good. Your wife is like a fruitful vine in the innermost parts of your home; your children are like olive plants around your table. Behold, so is blessed the man who fears Hashem. May Hashem bless you from Zion, and may you see the good of Jerusalem all the days of your life. May you see your children’s children, peace upon Israel.” ( Tehillim 128) Please, HaShem , as You hear every prayer, may the verse be fulfilled through me: "'As for Me,' says the Eternal One, "this, My Covenant, shall always be at the center of their being. My spirit, which rests upon you, and My words, which I have put in your mouth, shall not depart from your mouth nor from the mouths of your children, nor from the mouths of your children's children," says HaShem, "now and forever." May the words of my mouth and the thoughts of my heart be pleasing before You, HaShem, my Rock and my Redeemer. ( SHELAH HAKADOSH )

pages.title: Kosher Kitchen - Tevilas Keilim (Mikveh Immersion of Dining and Food Preparation Utensils) - Guidelines
pages.bodyText: Before using a new kitchen/dining utensil, it needs to be spiritually "acquired" by a Jewish owner. Utensil to be immersed must be completely clean – free of dirt, dust, rust, stickers, labels or glue. (Note: nail polish remover or WD-40 removes adhesive from stickers easily. Then rinse with dish soap and water.) At the mikveh : wet your hands in the mikvah water, hold the vessel in the wet hand and say the bracha (blessing): Baruch ata Adonoi, Eloheinu Melech haOlam, asher kidshanu b’mitzvosav v’tzivanu al tevilas keili ( keilim for multiple utensils). Then immerse the vessel(s). One blessing covers all the items to be immersed at that time. It's forbidden to repeat the bracha , and best not to speak until all items have been immersed. If you forgot to make the bracha , the immersion is still valid. The water of the mikveh must touch the entire vessel, inside and out. The entire vessel must be under water at one time, but does not have to be submerged for any specific amount of time. However, be careful that no air is trapped in the submerged vessels. Two or three seconds of swishing the item underwater is usually all the time that's needed for any trapped air bubbles to escape. If a basket or net is used to hold a number of small utensils (such as silverware), the basket should first be immersed in the water, the utensils placed in the basket, and the basket swirled under the water, so that the water will touch all areas of the utensils. Pot lids are immersed separately if they are removable. A pocket knife is immersed in its open position so that the water will touch all areas of the blade. Thermos bottle liners do not need to be removed before immersion. A narrow necked bottle is immersed neck up so that the inner surface of the bottle will fill completely with mikveh water. Anyone may tovel keilim , including a small child or a non-Jew. However, a Jewish adult must be present to verify that it took place. The bracha can only be said if a Jew does the immersion. Therefore, if many utensils are to be immersed with the help of a child or a non-Jew, the owner should first immerse a few vessels with a bracha and then the child or non-Jew can take over. Utensils require tevila with a bracha when they have direct contact with food during preparation or meal time and are made from metal such as aluminum, brass, copper, gold, iron, lead, silver, silverplate, steel, tin, or glass including pyrex, duralex, and corelle. According to A Practical Guide for Tevilas Keilim by Rabbi Mordechai Frankel: UTENSIL – TEVILAH Aluminum pan, disposable – Tevilah without a bracha if intended to be used only once; tevilah with a bracha if intended to be used more than once. Aluminum pan, non-disposable – Tevilah with a bracha . Apple corer (metal) – Tevilah with a bracha . Baking/Cookie sheet – Tevilah with a bracha . Barbecue grill - Racks require tevilah with a bracha , other components do not require tevilah . Blech – No tevilah . Blender /Mixer Glass or metal bowl, metal blades and other attachments require – tevilah with a bracha , other components do not require tevilah . Handheld immersion blender requires tevilah with a bracha . Bottle (metal or glass) – Tevilah with a bracha . If bought filled with food and subsequently emptied by a Jew, it does not require tevilah . Brush (grill, egg yolk, pastry) – No tevilah . Cake plate (metal or glass) – Plate needs tevilah with a bracha . Cake plate cover does not require tevilah . Can (metal or glass) – Tevilah with a bracha . If bought filled with food and subsequently emptied by a Jew, does not require tevilah . Can opener – No tevilah . Cast iron pot – Tevilah with a bracha . Ceramic knife – Tevilah without a bracha . Challah board – Metal board, or glass top on wooden board, requires tevilah with a bracha . Wood board with a plastic top does not require tevilah . Cheese slicer (metal) – Tevilah with a bracha . China (glazed) – Tevilah without a bracha . Coffee grinder – No tevilah . Coffee maker (electric) – No tevilah if it will break if immersed, otherwise requires tevilah with a bracha . Colander (metal) – Tevilah with a bracha . Cookie cutter – No tevilah (if only used with food that is not edible). Cookie sheet (metal) – Tevilah with a bracha . Cooling rack (metal) – Tevilah without a bracha . Corelle plate – Tevilah with a bracha . Corkscrew – No tevilah . Corningware – Tevilah without a bracha . Corn skewers (metal prongs) – Tevilah with a bracha . Crock pot – Metal or glass insert requires tevilah with a bracha , ceramic insert requires tevilah without a bracha , heating element does not require tevilah ; glass lid requires tevilah with a bracha . Cup/Mug – Tevilah with a bracha . If metal or glass, tevilah without a bracha if glazed ceramic, no tevilah if plastic. Cupcake/muffin pan (metal) – Tevilah with a bracha . Cutlery made of metal (forks knives, spoons) – Tevilah with a bracha . Knife used for arts and crafts only does not require tevilah . Cutting board (metal or glass) – Tevilah with a bracha . Dentures – No tevilah . Dishes – Tevilah with a bracha if metal or glass; tevilah without a bracha if glazed ceramic. Dish rack – No tevilah . Egg slicer (metal) – Tevilah with a bracha . Flour sifter – No tevilah . Frying pan (metal) – Tevilah without a bracha if Teflon coated, with a bracha if not coated. George Foreman grill – Tevilah without a bracha . Does not require t evilah if it will break if immersed. Glasses (metal or glass) – Tevilah with a bracha . Grater (metal) – Tevilah with a bracha . Grill – See Barbecue grill. Hot plate/Platta – No tevilah . Ice cream scooper (metal) – Tevilah with a bracha . Immersion blender – tevilah with a bracha . Metal blades and other attachments require tevilah with a bracha . Immersion heater – No tevilah . Kettle (metal or glass) – Tevilah with a bracha . Keurig machine – No tevilah if it will break if immersed, otherwise requires tevilah with a bracha . Kiddush cup (metal) – Tevilah with a bracha . Does not require tevilah if manufactured in Israel, but does require tevilah if sold in Israel and manufactured elsewhere. Knife sharpener – No tevilah . Ladle (metal) – Tevilah with a bracha . Measuring spoon (metal) – Tevilah without a bracha . Meat grinder (metal) – Attachments require tevilah with a bracha (if only used for raw meat: tevilah without a bracha ). Meat tenderizer(metal hammer) – No tevilah . Meat thermometer – No tevilah . Medicine spoon (metal or glass) – Tevilah without a bracha if used only for medicine. Melon baller (metal) – Tevilah with a bracha . Microwave turntable (glass) – Tevilah without a bracha . Nutcracker – Tevilah with a bracha if used at the table. Tevilah without a brocha, if not used at the table. Oven rack – No tevilah . See Toaster oven. Peppermill – Tevilah without a bracha . Peeler – Requires tevilah with a bracha if blade is metal, even if the rest of the unit is plastic. Plastic utensil – No tevilah . Popcorn maker (metal) – Tevilah with a bracha . It does not require tevilah if it will break if toveled. Pot (metal or glass) – Tevilah with a bracha . If Teflon, enamel or plastic coated, requires tevilah without a brocha. Pot cover (metal or glass) – Tevilah with a bracha . Pyrex cookware – Tevilah with a bracha . Roasting pan (metal) – Tevilah with a bracha . Rolling pin – No tevilah . Salt shaker (metal or glass) – Tevilah with a bracha . Metal cap on a plastic salt shaker requires tevilah without a bracha . Sandwich maker – Tevilah without a bracha . Scissors/Shears – Tevilah with a bracha if used for edible food. If only used for raw food, requires, tevilah without a brocha. Sieve (metal) – Tevilah with a bracha . Silicone bakeware or cookware – No tevilah . Sink rack – No tevilah . Skewer (metal) – Tevilah with a bracha . Spoon rest – No tevilah . Storage container – No tevilah Tevilah with a bracha . Teflon coated pan (metal) – Tevilah without a bracha . Thermos (metal or glass) with no insert – Tevilah with a bracha . Casing of thermos which has an insert does not require tevilah , and insert (metal or glass) requires tevilah with a bracha . Toaster – Tevilah without a bracha . Toaster oven – Rack and tray require tevilah , other components do not. Trivet – No tevilah if food does not touch the surface. Urn (metal) – Tevilah with a bracha . Waffle maker – Tevilah without a bracha . Warming tray – No tevilah . Washing cup (metal) – No tevilah if used only for washing hands. Wooden cask – No tevilah . Requires tevilah without a bracha if it has metal straps. 1. רבו הדעות בדין טבילת כלי העשוי לשמוש חד פעמי, עי’ בשו”ת אגרות משה יו”ד ח”ג סי’ כג ושו”ת מנחת יצחק ח”ה סי’ לב ושו”ת חלקת יעקב יו”ד סי’ מו ושו”ת חשב האפוד ח”ג סי’ ע ושו”ת שלחן הלוי פכ”ד אות לה וספר אשרי האיש יו”ד פ”ט אות ג ואות ד, ומש”כ בפנים הוא דעת מו”ר ר’ היינעמאן שליט”א. 2. ערוך השלחן יו”ד סי’ קכ סעי’ כג ושו”ת אג”מ יו”ד ח”ג סי’ כב וספר אשרי האיש יו”ד פ”ט אות ה, וע”ע בזה באמת ליעקב על שו”ע יו”ד סי’ קכ ובחלקת בנימין שם סעי’ א ביאורים ד”ה ‘מתכות’ ובספר טבילת כלים פי”א הערה קיג. 3. שו”ת אגרות משה יו”ד ח”ב סי’ מ וסוף סי’ קלז, אמנם עי’ בטבילת כלים פ”ד הערה טו בשם הגרש”ז אויערבאך זצ”ל ושם הערה כ מהגר”ח קניבסקי שליט”א בשם החזו”א ובשו”ת חלקת יעקב יו”ד סי’ מב ושו”ת ציץ אליעזר ח”ח סי’ כו וחלקת בנימין סי’ קכ ס”ק צב. 4. עי’ בחי’ רע”א יו”ד סי’ קכ על הש”ך ס”ק ד וערוך השלחן שם סעי’ כט, ועי’ מש”כ באמת ליעקב סי’ קכ הערה 52 לגבי כלי חרסינה של ימינו, ועי’ בשו”ת שלחן הלוי להגר”י בעלסקי שליט”א פכ”ד סעי’ לב הערה ה’ תהליך עשיית הציפוי לכלי חרסינה בימינו, ופסק שם שגם בימינו יש לטבול כלי חרסינה המצופה בגליזיר”ט בלי ברכה, וכן פסק מו”ר הר’ היינעמאן שליט”א. 5. מו”ר ר’ היינעמאן שליט”א אמר שאם בודאי יתקלקל הכלי ע”י טבילה וא”א לטבלו ולהשתמש בו אח”כ, א”כ הרי הוא אנוס שא”א לקיים המצוה, וכיון שכל האיסור להשתמש בכלי מאכל בלי טבילה נובע מהחיוב דאורייתא לטבלו א”כ במקום שפטור מטבילה מחמת אונס שוב מותר להשתמש בכלי זה לכתחלה. 6. עי’ בש”ך סי’ קכ ס”ק יא שכלי שמתקנים בו אוכל ועדיין צריך האוכל תיקון אחר חייב בטבילה בלא ברכה, ואם הכלי הזה א”א להשתמש בו למאכל אחר כמו הברזלים שמתקנים בהם המצות א”צ טבילה כלל, אבל הט”ז שם ס”ק ז כתב שדינם כסכין של שחיטה שכתב הרמ”א שטוב לטובלו בלא ברכה, וגם בביאור הגר”א שם ס”ק יד השיג על הש”ך. והפר”ח שם ס”ק יג פסק שהברזילים אינם צריכים טבילה (מטעם אחר של הש”ך, עיי”ש), והחכמת אדם כלל עג סעי’ ט פסק כדעת הש”ך, ואמר מו”ר 9. עי’ בספר טבילת כלים פי”א אות עז*. 10. שו”ת יביע אומר ח”ו יו”ד סי’ יב וספר אשרי האיש יו”ד פ”ט אות ט וספר טבילת כלים פרק יא הערה ל. 11. עי’ בחי’ רע”א סי’ קכ על הרמ”א סעי’ א מש”כ בזה, ועי’ ביד אפרים pages.title: Matchmaker's Chair
pages.bodyText: WELCOME to "Matchmaker's Chair"! If you’re drawn to Breslov teachings and not yet married, you’re invited to join "The Matchmaker's Chair." Simply complete the registration form below so you can receive a more detailed application by email. IMPORTANT: Your responses are seen only by Rabbi Maimon and designated staff. "They brought me a chair, surrounded by fire. The whole world was traveling to see this chair – men, women, and children. Suddenly, as they returned from seeing the chair, they were all paired up as each one's soul mate was found... When I asked 'What shall I do for my livelihood?' I was told that I would be a matchmaker." – Rebbe Nachman of Breslov, describing a dream he had just before Rosh HaShanah 5569 (1808), Chayey Moharan 84 "Master of the Universe... have compassion and mercy on us and reveal to us the path that will lead each of us to our true marriage partners...." – Rabbi Nasan of Nemirov, Likutey Tefilos II:45

pages.title: Prayer for a Beautiful Esrog
pages.bodyText: May it be Your Will, HaShem Elokeynu , the G-d of our forefathers, that You bless all of the esrog (citron) trees to bear their fruit at the proper time, and that they bear esrogim that are well-formed, beautiful, and free of all blemish. May they be complete and with no deficiencies, not even pricked by a thorn. And may these esrogim be available for us and for everyone in Klal Yisrael , wherever they may be, to fulfill the mitzvah of taking with the lulav on the holiday of Sukkos , may it come to us with good life, and with peace, as You have written in Your Torah through Moshe Rabbeinu , Your servant, “And on the first day you shall take for yourselves a beautiful fruit of the tree, a palm frond, and a branch of a myrtle tree, and willow brook …” ( Vayikra 23:40). May it be Your Will, HaShem Elokeynu , the G-d of our forefathers, that You help us and assist us in this mitzvah of taking the arba minim (palm branch, myrtle, willow, and citron) in the proper manner, in its proper time, on the festival of Sukkos , may it come upon us for good life, and peace, with happiness and good-heartedness. We pray that You prepare for us a beautiful esrog free of deficiencies, complete, and kosher according to its laws. יהי רצון מלפניך ה‘ א-להינו וא-להי אבותינו, שתברך כל אילנות האתרוג להוציא פירותיהם בעתם, ויוציאו אתרוגים טובים יפים ומהדרים ונקיים מכל מום, ולא יעלה בהם שום חזזית, ויהיו שלמים ולא יהיה בהם שום חסרון ואפילו עקיצת קוץ, ויהיו מצויים לנו ולכל ישראל בכל מקום שהם, לקיים בהם מצות נטילה עם הלולב בחג הסכות שיבא עלינו לחיים טובים ולשלום, כאשר צויתנו בתורתך על ידי משה עבדך, ”ולקחתם לכם ביום הראשון פרי עץ הדר כפות תמרים וענף עץ עבות וערבי נחל“ - ויקרא: כ“ג, מ ויהי רצון מלפניך ה‘ א-להינו וא-להי אבותינו, שתעזרנו ותסיענו לקים מצוה זו של נטילת לולב הדס ערבה ואתרוג, כתקנה בזמנה בחג הסכות שיבא עלינו לחיים טובים ולשלום בשמחה ובטוב לבב, ותזמין לנו אתרוג יפה ומהדר ונקי ושלם וכשר כהלכתו

pages.title: New Courses Page
pages.bodyText: Rabbi Maimon's courses in Breslov chassidus are based on traditional texts. Dialogue and questions are what Torah learning is all about, so let us know who you are, what you'd like to hear about, and how it's going via the CONTACT page. We're here for you ! A "course" page brings you short highlights of classes which link to the entire shiur if you'd like to hear more. Aitzos HaMevuoros - Faith Aitzos HaMevuoros – Advice Clarified – was written by a great-grandson of Rebbe Nachman of Breslov, Rabbi Shimshon Barsky. It’s a treasury of practical guidance about the basics of emunah (Jewish faith in Hashem and in His Torah) and how to implement Breslov chassidus into daily life. This series of five lectures was given by Rabbi Nasan Maimon in Jerusalem beginning on Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5775 (2015-04-20). Listen to Shiurim Azamra - The Good Point “ Azamra “(I will sing) is the name of Likutey Moharan Torah 282 — one of Rebbe Nachman’s most fundamental teachings. It’s about finding the “good point” in others, and in ourselves. Appreciating our own unique abilities to be aware of Hashem helps us serve Him with joy, day by day. Listen to Shiurim Breslov Basics - Mini Clips Listen to Shiurim Breslov Biographies - Mini Clips Listen to Shiurim Breslov Nigunim (Melodies) Listen to Shiurim Calendar Listen to Shiurim Deepening Faith Listen to Shiurim Eretz Yisrael Listen to Shiurim Ezras Nashim: Breslov Torah for Women Here we’ll be linking you to Breslov teachings especially relevant to women. Listen to Shiurim Halakha and Customs - Rabbi Rosenfeld ז"ל Listen to Shiurim Hebrew/Yiddish Listen to Shiurim Hisbodedus Listen to Shiurim Hishtapkhus - Outpouring of the Soul Hishtapkhus HaNefesh (Outpouring of the Soul) is a collection of Rabbi Nachman’s teachings about Hisbodedus – literally “seclusion” – voluntary prayer in one’s own words in addition to strengthen, enrich, and empower the individual’s emotional connection to the traditional mandatory prayers from the siddur (Jewish prayer book). The text is translated into and explained in English by Rabbi Nasan Maimon. The sefer was compiled by Rabbi Moshe Yehoshua Bezhilianski (known as Reb Alter of Teplik) and first published in Jerusalem about 1904. Reb Alter was born in Teplik, Ukraine, and was the son-in-law of one of Rav Nosson of Nemirov’s closest students, Reb Nachman Chazan. He became a leading teacher of Breslov chassidus throughout Europe and Russia by writing, publishing, and distributing a number of works about the teachings of Rabbi Nachman. In the words of Rabbi Aryeh Kaplan z”l : “ provides a path through which even the most unlearned Jew can find his way back to God.” Listen to Shiurim Parnassah - Livelihood Listen to Shiurim Sefer Tehillim Listen to Shiurim Shabbos Listen to Shiurim Shalom Bayis - Family Peace Listen to Shiurim Siddur (Traditional Jewish Prayers) Listen to Shiurim Simcha - Joy Welcome to a journey that will transform your life for the better! True and lasting happiness is not a mood that can be affected by events, relationships, or material possessions. It’s an ongoing series of quiet accomplishments that only you and Hashem can see. Rebbe Nachman of Breslov taught: “It’s a great mitzvah to always be happy…” ( Likutey Moharan 2:24). The question is: how? Rabbi Maimon has culled from a number of Breslov sources to guide you on the path that doesn’t simply lead you to some distant, better place. The path itself is that better place! Listen to Shiurim Sipurey Masiyos - The 13 Stories This series of lectures presents the Sipurey Masiyos ( The 13 Stories ) of Rebbe Nachman of Breslov as explained in English by Rabbi Nasan Maimon. Characters personify qualities within every Jewish soul. These mystical allegories contain some of the Torah’s deepest secrets and were originally published in Yiddish so women and children could enjoy and benefit from them. Listen to Shiurim Tefilah - Prayer Listen to Shiurim Tehillim Listen to Shiurim Tzaddik Finding and receiving from a spiritual guide is essential in Torah-true living. Here you will find stories about the lives of Am Yisrael’s Tzaddikim as well as selections from the Likutey Halakhos that explain the concept of “Tzaddik”. Speakers: Rabbi Zvi Aryeh Rosenfeld zal and Rabbi Nasan Maimon. Listen to Shiurim
